title: Console walkthrough: usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdown - Bluecrest Systems
summary: Redwood AE/SE ran a console-focused walkthrough for Bluecrest Systems showing usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and the cost breakdown features. Discussion covered hosted vs dedicated, VPC/KMS requirements, token-level cost attribution, and pilot sizing. Customer requested pricing, security docs, and a short pilot with a per-route cost baseline. Follow-ups agreed at the end.
action_items: Maya: Send pricing sheet and Dedicated SKU options - due 2026-03-27
Carlos: Share pilot runbook + recommended benchmark prompts and scripts - due 2026-03-30
Priya: Provide VPC architecture diagram and compliance checklist from Bluecrest - due 2026-03-29
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing and security pack (SOC2 summary, KMS integration doc)
Schedule 2-week pilot to measure per-route cost with 50k tokens/day target
SE to run an initial benchmark on Redwood hosted vs Dedicated and share results
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Bluecrest - Head of ML), Priya Shah (Bluecrest - Cloud Architect), Jordan Matthews (Bluecrest - PM)

Summary: Quick console demo focused on cost attribution and per-route dashboards, followed by Q&A around dedicated capacity and security requirements.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on the account, and Carlos is our SE. We'll walk through the Redwood Console—usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and the cost breakdown flow.
[00:27] Liam: Great, thanks. Quick context: we've been running a mix of LLM workloads — chat assistants and reranking. Cost has been spiking and we need better per-route visibility. We also have a tentative timeline to pick a vendor by end of Q2.
[01:15] Carlos: Awesome. At a high level, Console gives token-level cost attribution and per-route dashboards, so you can see cost by endpoint, model, and even prompt template. We'll show how that maps to batch size and caching.
[03:00] Maya: First slide is the Usage Overview — this is the main dashboard showing total tokens, P50/P95 latency, and cost over time. You can break down by model or by route.
[06:20] Carlos: I'll share my screen — apologies if the label shows "Redwood internal" — there is an option to filter by route path, model name, and timeframe. You can also compare two time ranges.
[08:05] Priya: Do you show cost back to individual routes? Like our /chat vs /embed endpoints?
[08:20] Carlos: Yes, each route gets a per-route dashboard. It includes tokens in/out, average tokens per request, cost per token metric, and aggregated spend. You can drill down to see top prompts contributing to spend. Note: there's some noise where the auto-transcription labels can be off, so in longer runs we rely on token hashing rather than transcribed text.
[10:00] Jordan: Can we map to our internal product tags? We have feature flags and want spend by feature.
[10:15] Carlos: You can pass a route tag in the SDK or set tags in the API calls. We ingest those tags and they appear in the dashboard. We also support custom attributes for billing export to S3 or BigQuery.
[12:30] Maya: On the right there's a Cost Breakdown panel — it attributes cost by model variant, then by route, and you can toggle to show latency costs vs raw token costs.
[15:00] Liam: How accurate is the token accounting if you do batching and KV-cache warmups? Our retriever pipeline does many short prefix calls which make caching behaviour important.
[15:25] Carlos: Good question. We show both raw token counts and an effective token metric that accounts for prefix/KV cache hits. When a request hits the KV cache, the incremental token cost appears lower. Also batching will change per-request token overhead; the UI shows adjusted cost per effective token. We can provide the exact formula — it's in the docs but I'll paste the link after the call (link: https://redwood.example.com/docs/console-cost-model).
[18:40] Priya: About Dedicated vs Hosted — our security team prefers Dedicated with a VPC for data control. How much different will the cost breakdown be?
[19:00] Maya: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and some per-GPU cost differences. The Console cost dashboards look the same for both modes — the main difference is the base infrastructure cost you're committing to. For quick pilots hosted often shows lower initial cost since you don't reserve capacity.
[20:30] Jordan: Any talk about auto-fallbacks and rollouts? We sometimes need canarying between model variants.
[20:50] Carlos: Yes, the rollout dashboard shows traffic split across model variants and routes. You can set canary policies and automatic fallback to cheaper variants when latency spikes. The cost impact is shown in the same per-route view.
[24:00] Liam: On security: SSO, audit logs, and KMS? Priya will likely want details.
[24:15] Maya: We support SAML SSO, RBAC in the console, and audit logs with export. For encryption we integrate with customer KMS/HSM and provide key rotation docs. I'll attach the SOC2 summary and KMS integration doc after this meeting.
[26:30] Priya: For VPC, do you have an on-prem option or is it only VPC peering?
[26:45] Carlos: We support both VPC peering and a private control plane option. For highly regulated customers we can ship a private deployment package. There are some differences in telemetry retention and how logs are exported; we'll share the architecture notes (note: link to VPC deployment notes).
[28:00] Maya: Back to the Console — here's the per-route trend view. You can see tokens per minute and the rolling cost. We'll filter to show only routes tagged "chat-prod".
[30:15] Carlos: If you click into a single request sample we show the prompt, model chosen, token count, and a small cost breakdown. Note there's occasional mis-attribution in the transcription of route names — that's UI-only, the underlying metrics are keyed by route id.
[33:00] Jordan: Curious about how we do chargeback to product teams. Can we export per-route spend daily?
[33:20] Carlos: Yes, daily exports to S3 or BigQuery with per-route rows. You can run scheduled jobs to import into your internal chargeback system. We also have a CSV export from the dashboard.
[36:00] Liam: For the pilot we'd want baseline numbers for our top 3 routes. What would Redwood need from us to run a bench?
[36:20] Carlos: Sample prompt sets, expected QPS per route, and preferred models. We usually ask for a small test dataset and a short run (24-72 hours) to measure P50/P95 latency and cost. We'll provide a runbook with scripts.
[38:30] Priya: Is there native integration with our billing system? We use internal charge codes.
[38:45] Maya: You can attach metadata tags per request and include cost exports. For Dedicated we can add custom billing SKUs in the contract.
[40:00] Jordan: Any competitors do better at per-route granularity? We've seen some dashboards from Anthropic partner dashboards but not token-level cost.
[40:15] Maya: From what we've seen, a lot of vendors show usage metrics but not token-level cost attribution tied to route and prompt templates. That's a Redwood differentiator — along with batching and KV-aware cost adjustments.
[42:00] Liam: Does the Console show cost impact of quantization or model compression?
[42:20] Carlos: We expose model profile differences: e.g., 8-bit quantized variant shows different per-token execution cost. The Console will show historical cost if you roll a quantized variant and compare.
[44:00] Priya: For compliance, can you provide redaction options for logs? We cannot retain PII in raw prompts.
[44:20] Carlos: We have redaction hooks and can redact/skip storing raw prompts. We also support redacted audit logs and allow you to export only metadata. We'll include the redaction docs in the security pack.
[46:30] Maya: Quick demo of the cost-forecast widget — you can project monthly spend based on current traffic and set alerts if spend exceeds thresholds.
[48:00] Jordan: Perfect. That helps our PMs plan.
[49:00] Liam: Ok, to recap our immediate asks: pricing for dedicated vs hosted, pilot runbook and scripts, security docs (SOC2 + KMS + redaction).
[49:30] Maya: Correct. We'll send pricing and security docs by Friday. Carlos will share the pilot runbook and benchmark scripts. Priya will send a VPC diagram and list of compliance controls they need.
[50:30] Priya: We'll aim to provide the VPC diagram by Monday.
[51:00] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the pilot kickoff.
[51:30] Call ended.

Artifacts referenced:
- Pilot runbook (post-call link: https://redwood.example.com/pilot-runbook)
- Console cost model doc (https://redwood.example.com/docs/console-cost-model)
- Security pack (SOC2 summary, KMS integration) — to be attached by Maya

Notes on transcription: occasional proper noun errors (e.g., "kv cache" transcribed as "K-V cash"), timestamps are approximate.
